title: How Saints hear living prayers—opinions vary; Costerus: by angels, migrants, and divine revelation for their glory
source_text: XLI. Quomodo vero Sancti orationes viventium audiant atque percipiant, res non est inter eos certa & definita, sed de qua varii varie opinantur. Costerus in Enchiridio dicit dubium non esse, quin Sancti in coelis cognoscant, quae in terris gerimus internunciis Angelis, & iis qui ex hac vita migrant: praesertim vero quin divina revelatione ipsis innotescant quae ad ipsorum gloriam promovendam ab hominibus fiunt. Deus enim qui Sanctorum suorum perfectum gaudium desiderat, nihil eorum ipsos celare, quae aliquo modo vel augere id, vel perficere possunt: Ejusmodi vero esse orationes, quae ad ipsos a viventibus effunduntur, & quaecunque in ipsorum gloriam ab iisdem suscipiuntur.
pass_a_gloss: But how the Saints hear and perceive the prayers of the living is not among them a certain and defined matter, but one on which various men variously opine. Costerus in the Enchiridion says it is not doubtful that the Saints in heaven know what we do on earth by angel messengers and by those who migrate from this life: and especially that by divine revelation there become known to them the things which men do to promote their glory. For God, who desires the perfect joy of His Saints, conceals from them nothing of those things which can in some way either increase or perfect that joy: and of that kind are the prayers which are poured out to them by the living, and whatsoever things are undertaken by the same for their glory.
pass_b_english: How Saints hear the living’s prayers is unsettled among Roman doctors.
Costerus: heaven knows earthly deeds by angel messengers and by the newly departed—and especially by revelation of what advances the Saints’ glory.
God hides from them nothing that can heighten that joy; living prayers and glory-works belong to that class.

choices.why: Named Roman locus for how Saints know earthly acts.
